newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open steady, focus on small caps.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open steady, focus on small caps.

text.p: Singapore shares were steady at the open on Wednesday with much of the activity centred on smaller issues.
Dealers said the market undertone was still firm though not as bullish as on Tuesday.
"Most of the shares are holding on to their overnight gains but they are also not moving up like yesterday," a broker with a Singapore brokerage said.
After about an hour, the Straits Times Industrial index was up 2.57 points to 2,058.25. Total market volume was over 33 million shares with 65 gainers against 67 losers.
Electronics stock MMI Holdings topped the actives list with over 3.3 million shares changing hands, including a 2.4 million block trade. It was down one cent to Singapore $0.72.

Uraco recovered slightly in active trade, rising 2.5 cents to S$0.845. The company had been under selling pressure for its exposure to CAM International which is being probed by the Commercial Affairs for alleged fraud.

Diversified book distributor Jack-Chia MPH was active and rose two cents to S$1.56. A dealer said there was no fresh news in the market regarding the company but someone was obviously collecting the shares.
